name: network
description: The network policy as the proxy of a sandbox applies it: the forms of a host a rule accepts and the ones it applies, deny against allow for the rules of a sandbox and for those of its kits, the rules of two mixins composed, and the check of the policy against the rules of a sandbox. Dummy hosts under example.invalid only: none resolves, so that nothing leaves the machine and a 403 is the answer of the policy.

scenarios.name: probe-np-default
args: for h in audit-net-plain.example.invalid a.audit-net-wild.example.invalid audit-net-port.example.invalid audit-net-scheme.example.invalid audit-net-path.example.invalid; do printf '%s %s\n' "$h" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 "http://$h/path/x")"; done
scenarios.note: every dummy host is allowed by default-allow-all: the proxy answers with its own error for a host that does not resolve, never 403

scenarios.name: deny-np-forms
scenarios.note: one deny rule per form a host can be written in: plain, wildcard, with a port, with a scheme, with a path

scenarios.name: policy-ls-np
scenarios.note: the resources as the daemon stored them

scenarios.name: probe-np-forms
args: for h in audit-net-plain.example.invalid a.audit-net-wild.example.invalid audit-net-port.example.invalid audit-net-scheme.example.invalid audit-net-path.example.invalid; do printf '%s %s\n' "$h" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 "http://$h/path/x")"; done
scenarios.note: 403 where a deny rule applies: the forms that do not apply are accepted all the same

scenarios.name: check-np-plain-global
scenarios.note: the check of the policy, for a host a rule of audit-np denies

scenarios.name: probe-nq
args: for h in audit-net-allowed.example.invalid audit-net-other.example.invalid; do printf '%s %s\n' "$h" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 "http://$h/path/x")"; done
scenarios.note: whether an allow rule, by host or by HTTP request, reopens a host for a sandbox whose rules deny **

scenarios.name: create-nk
scenarios.note: two mixins: one denies ** and allows a host, the other allows another host

scenarios.name: policy-ls-nk
scenarios.note: how the rules of the two mixins are composed

scenarios.name: probe-nk
args: for h in audit-net-allowed.example.invalid audit-net-extra.example.invalid audit-net-other.example.invalid; do printf '%s %s\n' "$h" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 "http://$h/path/x")"; done
scenarios.note: whether the allow rules of the kits reopen their hosts under the deny of **

scenarios.name: policy-ls-network-after
scenarios.note: whether the rules go with their sandboxes
